Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph CILG OPINION NO. S. 202 FEB 12 2020 ATTY. ARNOLFO RICARDO B. CABLING President Social Housing Finance Corporation BDP Plaza, 8737 Paseo de Roxas Makati City Dear Atty. Cabling: This has reference to your letters, both dated 30 October 2019, requesting for the Department's legal opinion on whether or not the open spaces of high density housing projects can be donated to the local government unit for purposes of establishing a police sub-station and public school, considering that Republic Act No. 10633 or the General Appropriations Act (GAA) for 2014 expressly provides that the appropriation therein for the housing program for informal settler families residing in danger areas within metro manila shall be used exclusively for the following projects: (i) Construction of Micro-Medium-Rise Building; and (ii) Interim Shelter Fund for 26,367 Target Families. Since the GAA for 2014 provides for the exclusivity on the use of the appropriated fund, you are now in a quandary on whether or not the open spaces of the housing projects funded under GAA for 2014 can be donated to the local government units of Naic, Cavite and Bacoor City, Cavite for purposes of establishing a police sub-station in South Morning View HDH Project and a public school in Ciudad De Strike Phase II — A HDH Project, respectively. Hence, your request. Foremost, DILG - Memorandum Circular No. 2015-561 provides for guidelines for the implementation of the Micro-Medium-Rise Building (MMRB) Projects. Item II(E) thereof guides us that the minimum requirements set forth in Batas Pambansa (BP) Blg. 2202 shall be observed. Section 33 of BP Blg. 220 allows the owner or project developer to donate the roads and open spaces found in the project to the local government of the area 1 Entitled, "GUIDELINES FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION OF DILG MICRO-MEDIUM-RISE BUILDING (MMRB) PROJECTS BY LGUs 2 Otherwise known as "An Act Authorizing the Ministry of Human Settlements to Establish and Promulgate Different Levels of Standards and Technical Requirements for Economic and Socialized Housing Projects in Urban and Rural Areas from Those Provided Under Presidential Decrees Numbered Nine Hundred Fifty-Seven, Twelve Hundred Sixteen, Ten Hundred Ninety-Six and Eleven Hundred Eighty-Five"

after their completion had been certified to by the Board and it shall be mandatory for the said local government to accept such donations. Henceforth, it is thus imperative to know the meaning of open spaces. Section 3 of BP Blg. 220 defined open spaces as referring to areas allocated for (a) Circulation; (b) Community Facilities; (c) Park/PIayground; (d) Easements; and (e) Courts. On the same Section, Community facilities is defined as pertaining to facilities or structures intended to serve common needs and for the benefit of the community, such as neighborhood/multipurpose center, drugstore, school, livelihood center, and the like. Thus, we are of the view that a police sub-station, similar with a school, is a community facility as it intends to serve common needs and for the benefit of the community. Moreover, the minimum design standards set forth are intended to provide minimum requirements within the generally accepted levels of safety, health and ecological considerations, such as, but not limited to protection and safety of life, limb, property and general public welfare3. While it is true that RA No. 10633 provides for the exclusivity on the use of the fund appropriated, we are of the view that open spaces is part and parcel of the socialized housing, which in this case is the housing program for informal settler families, and therefore, must conform to the minimum requirements provided in BP Blg. 220. Accordingly, the Department believes that the requested donation of open spaces for the provision of a police sub-station and public school may be granted. We hope we have addressed your concern accordingly. V E AR rul ours, . ANO Secretary CC: Dir. Elias F. Fernandez Regional Director DILG-Region IV-A Ls/90t€ 3 Section 5, BP Blg. 220 OILG-OSEC oa
